article_title: Knowledge, attitudes, and practices of pre-hospital emergency medical care practitioners regarding sepsis recognition: a cross-sectional study in Qatar.
citation: Lewis Michael Steven Paul, Smith Paula J. W., Howard Ian Lucas, Farhat Hassan, Alinier Guillaume. (2026). Knowledge, attitudes, and practices of pre-hospital emergency medical care practitioners regarding sepsis recognition: a cross-sectional study in Qatar. BMC Emergency Medicine. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12873-026-01607-7
title: 53-item KAP survey instrument with two scenario-based vignettes for sepsis recognition
description: A 53-item self-administered questionnaire developed through a three-stage process of literature synthesis, structured expert review with seven specialists, and pilot testing with frontline practitioners. It covers four domains — demographics (8 items), knowledge (18 items), attitudes (12 Likert-scale items), and practices (15 items) — and "included two scenario-based vignettes to assess applied knowledge in sepsis recognition". Content validity was supported by domain-level CVI values meeting or exceeding 0.78, and the attitude and practice scales showed good internal consistency (Cronbach's α = 0.89).
requirements: Expert review and pilot testing to establish content validity and face validity
constraints: Internal consistency findings should be interpreted as preliminary measures within this single-sample context
target_learners: Pre-hospital emergency medical care practitioners (paramedics, critical care assistants, critical care paramedics)
target_learning_goals: Assessing knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding sepsis recognition
examples: Scenario 1 assessed respondents' ability to recognise that the patient did not have sepsis, whereas Scenario 2 assessed recognition of sepsis in a more overt presentation
